title: Spanish A1–B1 Editorial Audit — The Teachers School

checks: All 18 lesson JSON files parse successfully.
Each unit contains two dialect variants.
Each unit variant contains five closed-choice exercises with valid answer indices.
All exercise IDs are unique within their variant.
A2 and B1 units contain ten dialogue turns and one original reading text per dialect variant.
A1 lesson variants contain 8–10 dialogue turns; A1 reading is supplied separately in spanish_a1_books.json.
No standalone vocabulary arrays remain in A1 lesson variants; vocabulary is embedded in context.
B1 correct-answer positions are distributed across options rather than fixed in the first position.

items: Corrected the Spain A1 family exercise to match the dialogue's singular sister reference and corrected the answer index.
Added merendar to the Spain daily-routine dialogue so the related comprehension item is grounded in context.
Added an explicit explanation of vosotros forms in the Spain food-ordering context; contrasted with ustedes in the Mexico route.
Simplified the Spain leisure dialogue and reduced consecutive Mexican colloquialisms in the Mexico dialogue.
Removed standalone vocabulary lists from all six A1 lesson units; vocabulary remains embedded in dialogues, grammar examples and exercises.
Corrected the Spain travel reading's temporal marker so pretérito perfecto is used with an unfinished current period.
Adjusted the Mexico travel dialogue to reflect the common use of pretérito indefinido for completed events while retaining pretérito perfecto for life experience.
Corrected an explanation that incorrectly attributed a visit with a sister to the Mexico travel dialogue.
Removed an unintroduced subjunctive construction from the Mexico health dialogue and simplified the corresponding Spain dialogue.
Made the hypothetical si + imperfecto de subjuntivo + condicional pattern explicit because it appears in the dialogue.
Aligned dialogues and reading passages with the grammar actually taught, removing or explaining unintroduced subjunctive and reported-speech forms.
Expanded the reported-speech explanation to include future → conditional and temporal-marker shifts.
Replaced generic comprehension and vocabulary questions with unit-specific questions grounded in each dialogue, reading and cultural note.
Corrected dialect-specific comprehension prompts and ensured the final dialogue turns are complete.
Distributed correct-answer positions across the three options to avoid a predictable answer pattern in B1 tests.

level_progression.A1: Foundational introductions, family, routine, food, city and leisure; present tense, descriptions, basic requests and plans.
level_progression.A2: Travel experience, household obligations, shopping, health, work and stories; perfect and past tenses, pronouns, comparisons and advice.
level_progression.B1: Decisions, personal change, media literacy, community, work projects and cultural identity; conditional hypotheses, pluscuamperfecto, subjunctive, se constructions and reported speech.

outstanding_work: Complete a final line-by-line language proofread by a qualified Spanish editor or native speaker for both dialect tracks.
Preview every selected A1 video/audio resource end-to-end and verify actual CEFR difficulty, regional language, availability in intended student regions and mobile playback.
Confirm commercial teaching, linking and embedding rights for each third-party media resource before any product integration.
Create media-specific original exercises only after reviewing the actual clips or recordings; do not infer answers from titles or summaries.
Record original Mexican Spanish audio for A1 units where no sufficiently clear and level-appropriate external source is confirmed.

integration.rule: Do not connect Spanish content to the Telegram bot or Learning Space until the complete Spanish catalog is finished, approved and media rights are checked.

positioning: These materials are a premium lead-magnet sample designed to demonstrate teaching quality and create motivation to book a trial lesson. They are not a complete CEFR course at each level.
